# prompts-to-skill-release

This skill takes a finished draft and makes it installable, tested and documented. It does not change the skill's behaviour. If a test fails, it goes back to tune-skill rather than editing the skill itself. Read `references/release-steps.md` for each step and `references/readme-template.md` for the README.

## Preconditions

Stop and report if any of these fail:

1. The skill folder exists, its name matches the `name` field and H1, and `check_skill.py` shows no FAIL.
2. `prompts-to-skill` has recorded its Gate A and Gate B results. A gate marked "written, not run" is a warning, not a pass.
3. The user has said what they want: a zip only, a GitHub repo, or both.

## Steps

**1. Test.** Run each case in `evals/evals.json` and each row in the tune-skill test-case table. Record pass, fail, or not-run for each. Never mark a case pass without running or reasoning through it against the real description. If you can only reason, say "reviewed, not executed".

**2. Fix or return.** For each failure, decide whether the fix is in the description (go back to tune-skill) or the body (go back to tune-skill as well). Do not edit the skill in this step. Re-run only the affected cases after tune-skill returns.

**3. Version.** Set `version: 0.1.0` in the frontmatter if there is none, and keep any existing version field unchanged. Add a `CHANGELOG.md` with one entry: what the skill does, the date, and the test results.

**4. Package.** Build the zip with the skill folder as the top-level entry, so unzipping gives `skill-name/SKILL.md`. Exclude `.DS_Store`, `__pycache__`, and any `evals/` results that contain personal data. Verify the archive with a listing.

**5. Discovery check.** Write three prompts that should trigger the skill and one that should not, using the user's own words. Judge each by reading the description. Record the result. Do not claim the skill is discoverable in a live session unless you tested it in one.

**6. README.** Write `README.md` from the template: what it does, install options, example prompts, the boundary with sibling skills, test results, and version. Keep the README out of the skill folder if the platform treats extra files as noise, and say which you chose.

**7. Install checklist.** Give the user the install steps for their platform: upload the zip in skills settings, or unzip into the skills directory, or use the `npx skills add` command if they publish to GitHub. Include a check to confirm the skill is visible.

**8. Publish (optional).** Only if the user asks. Create the repo, push the folder, and tag the version. Then hand off to `findable` for the name decision and listing, since that skill needs a live repo.

## Report

- Test results: counts for pass, fail, and reviewed-only.
- Files produced: zip, README, CHANGELOG, and their paths.
- Discovery result.
- Anything that needs the user's action, such as install or push.
- One next step.

## Boundaries

This skill packages and documents. It does not draft, tune, or name. Do not hide a failing test to make the release look clean. A failed test means the skill is not ready, and the report must say so.

# Release steps: detail

## Test execution

- Source of cases: `evals/evals.json` (`skill_name` plus an `evals` list of prompts) and the tune-skill test-case table (at least eight cases, including boundary pairs).
- For each case record: id, message, expected skill or mode, result (pass, fail, reviewed-only, not-run), and a one-line note.
- Pass condition is the one written in the table. Do not invent a looser one.
- Counts go in the report. If any case is not-run, say so in the first line of the report.

## Version

- Semantic version. The first release is 0.1.0.
- Do not change an existing `version` field to a different value. Bump only when the user asks, or when a release follows a tune-skill change.
- CHANGELOG entry format:

      ## 0.1.0 (YYYY-MM-DD)
      - Initial release from prompts: N prompts, M test cases.
      - Tests: X pass, Y fail, Z reviewed-only.

## Packaging

- Archive root is the skill folder. Example: `prompts-to-skill.zip` contains `prompts-to-skill/SKILL.md`.
- Exclude `.DS_Store`, `__pycache__`, `*.pyc`, and any file under `evals/` that holds real user data.
- Verify with `unzip -l` and confirm the SKILL.md path.

## Discovery check

- Three should-trigger prompts in the user's own words, no skill name.
- One should-not-trigger prompt that shares keywords with the description.
- Judge from the description text only. Record that this was a read-through, not a live session.

## Install by platform

- Claude app or web: upload the zip through the skills settings.
- Claude Code: copy the folder into `~/.claude/skills/` or the project's `.claude/skills/`.
- Qoder: copy the folder into `~/.qoder/skills/<name>/`, then reload skills or start a new session.
- Other agents: copy into the directory that agent reads (`.agents/skills/`, `.cursor/skills/`, and similar), per its docs.
- GitHub installs: `npx skills add <owner>/<repo> --skill <name>`.
- Always end with a check: the skill appears in the agent's skill list.

---
name: keyword-resolver
description: Resolve keyword cannibalization with Keyword-Guard, then generate alternative titles/H1/meta descriptions with Wordsmith. Use when the user wants to eliminate internal competition between pages, assign query ownership from Search Console or sitemap, de-conflict mixed-language pages with hreflang, or build cluster maps — and wants both the diagnosis and concrete rewrite alternatives. Chains keyword-guard (audit) → wordsmith (alternatives) in one workflow. Not for technical SEO diagnosis (use seo-audit) or mass page generation (use programmatic-seo).
version: 1.0.0
argument-hint: "[target keywords | sitemap URL | GSC export]"
user-invocable: true
metadata:
  version: "1.0.0"
---

# Keyword-Resolver

Chain two existing skills into a single workflow: **Keyword-Guard** audits keyword cannibalization and assigns query ownership, then **Wordsmith** generates alternative titles, H1s, meta descriptions, and content adjustments that resolve internal competition while preserving search intent.

## Invocation

```text
/keyword-resolver [paste target keywords + current pages]
/keyword-resolver https://example.com/sitemap.xml
Resolve cannibalization for "agent skill" and "SEO audit".
```

If no target is provided, ask the user for either:
- A list of target keywords + the pages currently ranking for them
- A sitemap URL to inventory
- Search Console data (page + query export)

## Workflow

### Phase 1: Run Keyword-Guard Audit

Invoke the **Keyword-Guard skill** with the provided inputs:

1. If GSC access: query dimensions `page + query` for each target keyword, list every page ranking.
2. If no GSC: pull sitemap, inventory URLs by title/H1/body mentions, flag homepage vs sub-page conflicts.
3. Assign ownership: one query → one owner (most clicks/impressions, closest semantic match).
4. Identify cannibalization: pages sharing primary keyword in title+H1, mixed-language conflicts without hreflang.
5. Output: a structured ownership map with conflict findings and resolution plan.

**Handoff rule:** Capture keyword-guard's full audit output verbatim. Do not summarize yet.

### Phase 2: Generate Alternatives with Wordsmith

Pass keyword-guard's audit findings to the **Wordsmith skill** with this instruction:

```
For each cannibalization conflict identified below, generate 2–3 alternative versions
that resolve the competition while preserving search intent. Focus on:

- Title tags: rewrite non-owners to distinct long-tail modifiers
- H1 headings: de-optimize non-owners, keep owners aligned
- Meta descriptions: clarify unique value per page
- Content adjustments: strip competing primary keywords from non-owners
- Hreflang fixes: declare full reciprocal sets for multi-language pages

Original audit:
[Paste keyword-guard's full report here]

Target pages:
[List the specific URLs flagged for each conflict]
```

Wordsmith should:
- Treat each conflict as a separate rewrite task
- Provide 2–3 options per page (labeled Option A/B/C)
- Keep the author's voice and facts intact
- Highlight which option best resolves each cannibalization issue

### Phase 3: Present Results

Return a three-part response:

1. **Keyword-Guard Ownership Map** (one query → one owner, conflicts listed)
2. **Wordsmith Alternatives** (grouped by conflict, with options labeled per page)
3. **Recommended Actions** (which combination of alternatives to apply, plus internal linking changes, in 2–3 sentences)

Format the alternatives so the user can copy-paste directly into their CMS or HTML files.

## Example

```
User: /keyword-resolver "agent skill" and "SEO audit"

Assistant:

## Keyword-Guard Ownership Map

**Query: "agent skill"**
- Owner: /skills/findable-polish (12 clicks, 45 impressions)
- Competing: /skills/findable (8 clicks, 30 impressions), / (homepage, 5 clicks, 20 impressions)
- Conflict: All three share "agent skill" in title+H1

**Query: "SEO audit"**
- Owner: /skills/seo-audit (20 clicks, 60 impressions)
- Competing: /skills/keyword-guard (3 clicks, 10 impressions)
- Conflict: keyword-guard's title mentions "SEO audit" but it's not the owner

## Wordsmith Alternatives

### Conflict 1: "agent skill" — /skills/findable

**Option A:** Title: "Repo Discovery Audit for AI Agents" | H1: "Make Your Repos Findable by Agents"
**Option B:** Title: "GitHub Visibility Audit for Skills" | H1: "Audit Repo Discoverability Gaps"
**Option C:** Title: "Agent Skill Discovery Setup" | H1: "Set Up GitHub Discovery for Agent Skills"

→ Best: Option A (removes "agent skill" from title, keeps semantic relevance)

[... continues for each conflict ...]

## Recommended Actions

1. Apply Option A to /skills/findable title+H1.
2. Add internal link FROM /skills/findable TO /skills/findable-polish with anchor "workflow that polishes discoverability".
3. Rewrite /skills/keyword-guard title to "SEO Keyword Cluster Planner" to stop competing with seo-audit.
4. Declare hreflang set for /ar/skills/* if Arabic locale exists (currently missing return tags).
```

## Boundaries

- **Does not** execute technical crawl/index/perf diagnosis (use seo-audit for that).
- **Does not** generate mass template pages (use programmatic-seo for that).
- **Does not** change canonical tags across locales unless explicitly asked (cross-canonical suppresses indexing).
- **Does not** access GSC automatically — works from pasted exports or sitemap inventory.

## Dependencies

This skill requires both `keyword-guard` and `wordsmith` to be installed. If either is missing, tell the user and stop.

1	# keyword-resolver
2	
3	**Resolve keyword cannibalization and generate optimized alternatives.**
4	
5	When multiple pages on your site compete for the same search queries, keyword-resolver identifies the conflicts and fixes them. It runs Keyword-Guard to audit cannibalization (which pages compete, which should own which queries), then passes the findings to Wordsmith to generate alternative titles, H1s, and meta descriptions that de-conflict the pages. You get both the audit and the concrete rewrites.
6	
7	## Usage
8	
9	```text
10	/keyword-resolver [paste target keywords + current pages]
11	/keyword-resolver https://example.com/sitemap.xml
12	Resolve cannibalization for "agent skill" and "SEO audit".
13	```
14	
15	## When to use
16	
17	- Two pages rank for the same keyword and neither ranks well
18	- Search Console shows multiple pages getting impressions for one query
19	- You have mixed-language pages competing with each other
20	- Someone asks "which page should rank for X?"
21	- You want to build a keyword cluster map for your site
22	
23	## What it produces
24	
25	- A cannibalization audit showing which pages compete for which queries
26	- Query ownership assignments (one page per primary keyword)
27	- Alternative titles, H1s, and meta descriptions from Wordsmith
28	- hreflang recommendations for mixed-language sites
29	- A cluster map showing pillar/satellite relationships
30	
31	## Install
32	
33	```bash
34	npx skills add arm-pz/keyword-resolver
35	```
36	
37	## Not for
38	
39	- Technical SEO diagnosis → use [seo-crawl](https://github.com/arm-pz/seo-crawl) or [seo-polish](https://github.com/arm-pz/seo-polish)
40	- Mass page generation → use programmatic-seo (third-party, [marketingskills](https://github.com/coreyhaines31/marketingskills))
41	- General discoverability audit → use [findable-polish](https://github.com/arm-pz/findable-polish)
42	
43	## Related
44	
45	- **[keyword-guard](https://github.com/arm-pz/keyword-guard)** — Audit cannibalization (the diagnosis half)
46	- **[seo-polish](https://github.com/arm-pz/seo-polish)** — Full technical SEO audit + polished fixes
47	
48	## License
49	
50	MIT © Abdul Rahman P Z

# keyword-resolver

**Resolve keyword cannibalization and generate optimized alternatives.**

When multiple pages on your site compete for the same search queries, keyword-resolver identifies the conflicts and fixes them. It runs Keyword-Guard to audit cannibalization (which pages compete, which should own which queries), then passes the findings to Wordsmith to generate alternative titles, H1s, and meta descriptions that de-conflict the pages. You get both the audit and the concrete rewrites.

## Usage

```text
/keyword-resolver [paste target keywords + current pages]
/keyword-resolver https://example.com/sitemap.xml
Resolve cannibalization for "agent skill" and "SEO audit".
```

## When to use

- Two pages rank for the same keyword and neither ranks well
- Search Console shows multiple pages getting impressions for one query
- You have mixed-language pages competing with each other
- Someone asks "which page should rank for X?"
- You want to build a keyword cluster map for your site

## What it produces

- A cannibalization audit showing which pages compete for which queries
- Query ownership assignments (one page per primary keyword)
- Alternative titles, H1s, and meta descriptions from Wordsmith
- hreflang recommendations for mixed-language sites
- A cluster map showing pillar/satellite relationships

## Install

```bash
npx skills add arm-pz/keyword-resolver
```

## Not for

- Technical SEO diagnosis → use [seo-crawl](https://github.com/arm-pz/seo-crawl) or [seo-polish](https://github.com/arm-pz/seo-polish)
- Mass page generation → use programmatic-seo (third-party, [marketingskills](https://github.com/coreyhaines31/marketingskills))
- General discoverability audit → use [findable-polish](https://github.com/arm-pz/findable-polish)

## Related

- **[keyword-guard](https://github.com/arm-pz/keyword-guard)** — Audit cannibalization (the diagnosis half)
- **[seo-polish](https://github.com/arm-pz/seo-polish)** — Full technical SEO audit + polished fixes

| Message | Should trigger | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |

| "The draft is done, make it installable" | prompts-to-skill-release | input is a finished folder |

# Keyword-Resolver

Chain two existing skills into a single workflow: **Keyword-Guard** audits keyword cannibalization and assigns query ownership, then **Wordsmith** generates alternative titles, H1s, meta descriptions, and content adjustments that resolve internal competition while preserving search intent.

## Invocation

```text
/keyword-resolver [paste target keywords + current pages]
/keyword-resolver https://example.com/sitemap.xml
Resolve cannibalization for "agent skill" and "SEO audit".
```

If no target is provided, ask the user for either:
- A list of target keywords + the pages currently ranking for them
- A sitemap URL to inventory
- Search Console data (page + query export)

## Workflow

### Phase 1: Run Keyword-Guard Audit

Invoke the **Keyword-Guard skill** with the provided inputs:

1. If GSC access: query dimensions `page + query` for each target keyword, list every page ranking.
2. If no GSC: pull sitemap, inventory URLs by title/H1/body mentions, flag homepage vs sub-page conflicts.
3. Assign ownership: one query → one owner (most clicks/impressions, closest semantic match).
4. Identify cannibalization: pages sharing primary keyword in title+H1, mixed-language conflicts without hreflang.
5. Output: a structured ownership map with conflict findings and resolution plan.

**Handoff rule:** Capture keyword-guard's full audit output verbatim. Do not summarize yet.

### Phase 2: Generate Alternatives with Wordsmith

Pass keyword-guard's audit findings to the **Wordsmith skill** with this instruction:

```
For each cannibalization conflict identified below, generate 2–3 alternative versions
that resolve the competition while preserving search intent. Focus on:

- Title tags: rewrite non-owners to distinct long-tail modifiers
- H1 headings: de-optimize non-owners, keep owners aligned
- Meta descriptions: clarify unique value per page
- Content adjustments: strip competing primary keywords from non-owners
- Hreflang fixes: declare full reciprocal sets for multi-language pages

Original audit:
[Paste keyword-guard's full report here]

Target pages:
[List the specific URLs flagged for each conflict]
```

Wordsmith should:
- Treat each conflict as a separate rewrite task
- Provide 2–3 options per page (labeled Option A/B/C)
- Keep the author's voice and facts intact
- Highlight which option best resolves each cannibalization issue

### Phase 3: Present Results

Return a three-part response:

1. **Keyword-Guard Ownership Map** (one query → one owner, conflicts listed)
2. **Wordsmith Alternatives** (grouped by conflict, with options labeled per page)
3. **Recommended Actions** (which combination of alternatives to apply, plus internal linking changes, in 2–3 sentences)

Format the alternatives so the user can copy-paste directly into their CMS or HTML files.

## Example

```
User: /keyword-resolver "agent skill" and "SEO audit"

Assistant:

## Keyword-Guard Ownership Map

**Query: "agent skill"**
- Owner: /skills/findable-polish (12 clicks, 45 impressions)
- Competing: /skills/findable (8 clicks, 30 impressions), / (homepage, 5 clicks, 20 impressions)
- Conflict: All three share "agent skill" in title+H1

**Query: "SEO audit"**
- Owner: /skills/seo-audit (20 clicks, 60 impressions)
- Competing: /skills/keyword-guard (3 clicks, 10 impressions)
- Conflict: keyword-guard's title mentions "SEO audit" but it's not the owner

## Wordsmith Alternatives

### Conflict 1: "agent skill" — /skills/findable

**Option A:** Title: "Repo Discovery Audit for AI Agents" | H1: "Make Your Repos Findable by Agents"
**Option B:** Title: "GitHub Visibility Audit for Skills" | H1: "Audit Repo Discoverability Gaps"
**Option C:** Title: "Agent Skill Discovery Setup" | H1: "Set Up GitHub Discovery for Agent Skills"

→ Best: Option A (removes "agent skill" from title, keeps semantic relevance)

[... continues for each conflict ...]

## Recommended Actions

1. Apply Option A to /skills/findable title+H1.
2. Add internal link FROM /skills/findable TO /skills/findable-polish with anchor "workflow that polishes discoverability".
3. Rewrite /skills/keyword-guard title to "SEO Keyword Cluster Planner" to stop competing with seo-audit.
4. Declare hreflang set for /ar/skills/* if Arabic locale exists (currently missing return tags).
```

## Boundaries

- **Does not** execute technical crawl/index/perf diagnosis (use seo-audit for that).
- **Does not** generate mass template pages (use programmatic-seo for that).
- **Does not** change canonical tags across locales unless explicitly asked (cross-canonical suppresses indexing).
- **Does not** access GSC automatically — works from pasted exports or sitemap inventory.

## Dependencies

This skill requires both `keyword-guard` and `wordsmith` to be installed. If either is missing, tell the user and stop.

- Alternative titles, H1s, and meta descriptions from Wordsmith
- hreflang recommendations for mixed-language sites
- A cluster map showing pillar/satellite relationships

## Install

```bash
npx skills add arm-pz/keyword-resolver
```

## Not for

- Technical SEO diagnosis → use [seo-crawl](https://github.com/arm-pz/seo-crawl) or [seo-polish](https://github.com/arm-pz/seo-polish)
- Mass page generation → use programmatic-seo (third-party, [marketingskills](https://github.com/coreyhaines31/marketingskills))
- General discoverability audit → use [findable-polish](https://github.com/arm-pz/findable-polish)

## Related

- **[keyword-guard](https://github.com/arm-pz/keyword-guard)** — Audit cannibalization (the diagnosis half)
- **[seo-polish](https://github.com/arm-pz/seo-polish)** — Full technical SEO audit + polished fixes
